Subject: Autumn trails: a few things worth thinking through before you go
Preview: Daylight shrinks fast this time of year. A quick read before your next trip.
Body: Hey,

Fall hiking has a particular rhythm. The air is cooler, the crowds thin out, and the light goes golden in a way that makes you want to stay out longer than you should. That last part is where things can get complicated.

A few practical notes for autumn trail time:

**Daylight math matters more now.**
At 45° north latitude, you're losing roughly 2–3 minutes of usable light per day through October. If your turnaround plan was built around summer hours, it needs revisiting. Check your sunset time the night before, then subtract 30–45 minutes to account for tree cover and canyon shadow.

**Mud season is a real thing.**
Post-rain trails at elevation can stay saturated for days. Soft tread does measurable damage to wet trail surfaces. If a trail looks soupy, a lower-elevation alternative is worth the reroute — both for the trail and for your footing.

**Layer math shifts in autumn.**
Morning starts can be 20°F colder than midday temps at elevation. A base layer that works at 7 a.m. can leave you sweating by noon and cold again by 4 p.m. Plan your system around your coldest and warmest expected moments, not just one of them.

**Water sources get unreliable.**
Some springs and seasonal streams that ran strong in July are dry by September. Carry more than you think you need, or filter from the last confirmed source before your high point.

**Tell someone your plan.**
Not a reminder you need, but worth saying plainly: rescue response times in shoulder season can be longer because trail traffic is lighter and conditions vary more. A shared itinerary with a specific check-in time costs nothing.

We'll keep sending trip-focused notes through the season. If there's a specific terrain type or trip length you're planning around, reply and let us know — it helps us write things that are actually useful.

Get out there while the color lasts.

— The Northbay Supply team
